name: manual_94cbd6
claim: When 'gh'/'git push' auth fails with 'Invalid username or token', check for a stale env var matching the CLI's exact lookup name (GITHUB_TOKEN for gh/git) before assuming the stored credential is broken -- 'gh auth status' with that var unset reveals whether a working keyring-stored token is being shadowed; scope the fix to 'env -u GITHUB_TOKEN <cmd>' per-command rather than editing the secrets file that defines it.

decisions.notes: ~/.env defines a stale/invalid GITHUB_TOKEN that gh CLI and git both check before their keyring-stored credential, so every push attempted 'normally' failed with 'Authentication failed', even though 'gh auth status' showed a valid, active diazMelgarejo keyring token underneath it. Same shape as the earlier GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN-vs-CODEX_GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN naming mismatch found this same session on the MCP github plugin: an env var with the exact name a tool checks silently overrides a working credential, and the fix is scoping/unsetting per-invocation, never guessing or rewriting the secrets file blind.
